summary: Feed s130_double is degraded: 29.08 Gbps microbursts overload single 10 Gbps APM port (291% capacity, 1 interval) causing 2.6% TCP packet drops (199/7606 packets). APM loses transactions during bursts.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts up to 29.08 Gbps exceed the single 10 Gbps APM port and packet broker buffers, causing tail drops that appear as TCP sequence gaps (2.6% of packets). Drops correlate directly with tool_overload intervals, not SPAN/TAP misconfiguration.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees incomplete flows, retransmissions and truncated transactions; latency and error calculations are skewed and application performance visibility is incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Distributing flows across 3x10G APM ports scales capacity to ~30 Gbps to absorb 29 Gbps bursts and eliminates buffer drops while preserving both directions required by APM. Since APM needs_full_payload=false, optional slicing/filtering to VLANs 10,20 can further reduce load.

findings.root_cause: Single 10 Gbps APM port fed 29.08 Gbps peak in 1 ms burst (291% of capacity). No load balancing or aggregation to scale capacity for microbursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM port discards excess traffic during bursts, creating blind spots, loss of bidirectional flow correlation (needs_both_directions=true) and missed application transactions.

recommended_fix.why: Hash-based load balancing across multiple 10G APM ports (or 2-3 port LAG) provides ~30 Gbps headroom, preserves flow symmetry for APM, and prevents burst drops. Add broker buffering and consider slicing as APM does not need full payload.
